components/custom/tool-types/handle-styl:
{{> components/common/modal/popup-header }}

CHOOSING YOUR HANDLES

All LEVEL5 handles feature a robust, yet lighweight aluminium construction.

Fixed Length Handles: Ideal for everyday job site conditions when standard walls, ceilings etc. If selected, your set will include:

  • 4-712 - 42” Fixed Flat Box Handle
  • 4-779 - 54” Corner Finisher Handle
  • 4-778 - 50” Corner Applicator Handle
  • 4-777 - 54” Corner Roller Handle

Extendable Handles: If your job site conditions will vary dramatically, and you need added flexibility for reaching high walls & ceilings, or shrinking down to finish closets and tight spaces, consider selecting extension handles. If selected, your set will include:

  • 4-780 - 40” - 62” Extendable Flat Box Handle
  • 4-795 - 31” - 50” Extendable Corner Finisher Handle
  • 4-794 - 31” - 50” Extendable Corner Applicator Handle
  • 4-792 - 31” - 50” Extendable Corner Roller Handle
components/custom/tool-types/automatic-t:
{{> components/common/modal/popup-header }}

TAPE UP TO 300% FASTER.

If you’re planning to tackle large commercial or residential projects, an automatic taper will dramatically speed up your taping workflow. It applies both tape & mud at the same time making quick work of flat seams and inside corners.

When selected, it will automatically add a gooseneck to your tool set to ensure you can fill up your taper.

GET TO KNOW THE TAPER

Watch Scott Murray go over the design, build, and usage of the LEVEL5 Automatic Taper.
components/custom/tool-types/flat-box-st:
{{> components/common/modal/popup-header }}

STANDARD OR MEGA?

Standard: A classic flat box shape designed to balance weight and mud capacity.

MEGA: A larger flat box chassis that holds up to 30% more mud. This means fewer trips back and forth to the pump, but it will be heavier on the wall.

Similar Features:
  • Built from premium-grade anodized aluminum for corrosion resistance.
  • Adjustable crown dial helps you dial in the perfect mud application.
  • Proprietary urethane wiper seal makes for extremely smooth application.
Good-To-Knows:
  • Every compound pump includes a free flat box filler valve, so you will be able to efficiently fill any flat boxes you choose right out of the box.
  • Every flat box comes with two sets of springs. Depending on your preference, these springs can increase or decrease the push force when using your flat boxes, giving you more control.

VIDEO RESOURCES

Get familiar with the design & quality of LEVEL5 flat boxes, and explore how they are used in the field.
components/custom/tool-types/flat-box-si:
{{> components/common/modal/popup-header }}

FLAT BOX SIZES

10”/12”: The most common choice for professional finishers, the 10” flat box is a standard all-around choice for first & second coats. The 12” flat box is generally used for final finishing coats, covering a wider area and feathering out the mud. These sizes also require fewer trips to the pump, making them ideal for larger projects.

7”/10”: The 7” flat box is ideal for first coats, and those looking for a lighter box in the hand. With this set up, the 10” box acts as the tool for your final coats. This choice offers a lighter weight set up, and a slightly lower cost.

Similar Features:
  • Built from premium-grade anodized aluminum for corrosion resistance.
  • Adjustable crown dial helps you dial in the perfect mud application.
  • Proprietary urethane wiper seal makes for extremely smooth application.
Good-To-Knows:
  • Every compound pump includes a free flat box filler valve, so you will be able to efficiently fill any flat boxes you choose right out of the box.
  • Every flat box comes with two sets of springs. Depending on your preference, these springs can increase or decrease the push force when using your flat boxes, giving you more control.

VIDEO RESOURCES

Get familiar with the design & quality of LEVEL5 flat boxes, and explore how they are used in the field.
components/custom/tool-types/applicator-:
{{> components/common/modal/popup-header }}

CORNERS CONQUERED.

Your choice in corner applicator tools comes down to convenience, preference, and job type. Here’s a breakdown of the key differences:

Corner Applicator: A 7” all-aluminum, corrosion resistant housing featuring a proprietary urethane wiper seal. The key benefits are:

  • Lightweight on the wall
  • Manual mud control for those who want it
  • Lower upfront cost
  • Easy to clean & maintain

MiniShot: A pressurized compound applicator that delivers mud without the manual pushing of a backplate. During the filling process, back pressure is created that seamlessly dispenses mud with an adjustable flow when pressed onto the wall. The key benefits are:

  • Very fast and smooth operation for larger projects
  • No pushing on the wall, when the Minishot is activated the flow nozzle ensures consistent coverage.
  • Holds significantly more mud, meaning fewer trips back and forth to the pump and longer runs across the wall.
  • Less fatigue over long days.

VIDEO RESOURCES

Checkout these design overviews and usage videos!
components/custom/tool-types/corner-fini:
{{> components/common/modal/popup-header }}

CORNER FINISHERS

All LEVEL5 corner finishers feature a precision-machined aluminum body, premium color anodizing for corrosion resistance, and a robotically welded frame for long-term reliability. This choice comes down to flexibility and budget.

Single 3” Finisher: The most versatile size for a corner finisher, letting you achieve a professional finish and save time by applying mud to both sides of inside corners.

3” & 3.5” Finishers: To minimize sanding and touch ups, this grouping of finishers offers added feathering capabilities to your set. Use the 3” finisher for the initial tape “glazing” coat, and the 3.5” finisher for the second fill coat. The larger finisher will ensure corners are feathered out.
components/common/responsive-img: {{!-- This file implements the lazysizes srcset pattern (as seen on https://github.com/aFarkas/lazysizes#modern-transparent-srcset-pattern) for maximum performance on modern browsers and reasonable compatibility with legacy browsers. There are a few important arguments to know about when using this component: `lazyload`: - If set to 'lazyload+lqip', will load a low-res image which will be replaced by lazysizes - ensuring that SOME content is shown immediately on page load. Without LQIP, a transparent gif will be used instead, which reduces the number of requests needed to load the page, making it even faster. - If set to 'lazyload', the browser will not load the full-size image at first, instead the lazysizes plugin will load it progressively after page load. This improves the load speed of the page, but it should be disabled for high-priority above-the-fold images. - If set to 'disabled', will not attempt to lazyload the image and instead tell the browser to load it immediately. Use this for high-priority images that are above the fold. `fallback_size`: This is the size to use for this image in legacy browsers that do not support srcset. Can be defined as a pixel bounding-box size (e.g. "123x123) or inherent width (e.g. "123w"). `class`: The CSS classes to add to the image, e.g. "card-image". If lazyloading is enabled, all images will have the "lazyload" class so that lazysizes will target them automatically. `otherAttributes`: Any other HTML attributes you want on the img tag, for example "height='100' width='100'" `default_image`: The default image to use if `image` is undefined or falsy. Should be a theme asset, usually defined as a relative path in the theme config. If a default image is not provided, you'll get an image tag with no image if the primary image is undefined. `lqip_size`: If you want to specify a particular size for the LQIP image, you can do so with this argument.
